La scienza dei materiali e la tecnologia sono la nostra passione. Con la nostra ricerca all'avanguardia, i circa 1.100 dipendenti di Empa danno un contributo essenziale al benessere della società per un futuro che vale la pena di vivere. Empa è un'istituzione di ricerca del dominio ETH. PhD Position sulle batterie All-Solid-State I materiali di laboratorio di Empa per la conversione dell’energia si concentrano sull’innovazione dei materiali e dei dispositivi per le tecnologie energetiche sostenibili.
• I tuoi compiti L'obiettivo di questo progetto PhD è quello di indagare le batterie allo stato solido a base di litio e di sodio utilizzando le tecniche di caratterizzazione di massa e interfaccia a base di muon. L'obiettivo principale è quello di ottenere una comprensione meccanicistica delle prestazioni elettrochimiche, con un focus sui processi di distribuzione, trasporto e degrado dell'ione durante il funzionamento della batteria. Il progetto affronta questioni chiave come la formazione di gradienti di concentrazione di Li/Na durante la carica e lo scarico, l'evoluzione delle interfase e dei meccanismi di degrado tra cui l'invecchiamento, la dissoluzione dei materiali (leaching), e la migrazione dei metalli di transizione. I metodi a base di muon saranno utilizzati per sondare le proprietà recuperate in profondità che sono difficili da accedere con le tecniche convenzionali, consentendo nuove intuizioni nelle interfacce sepolte e nei fenomeni di trasporto in massa. Il vostro lavoro si concentrerà sulla caratterizzazione elettrochimica e strutturale dei materiali e delle cellule della batteria, combinati con esperimenti basati su muon. Progetterai e eseguirai esperimenti per identificare le vie di reazione e i meccanismi di degradazione, e analizzerai set di dati complessi per collegare processi microscopici con prestazioni macroscopiche. Una stretta collaborazione con i partner del progetto sosterrà lo sviluppo e la sperimentazione di materiali e concetti cellulari. Il tuo profilo Hai un Master in chimica, scienza dei materiali, o un campo correlato, l'esperienza in elettrochimica o batterie è un vantaggio. Sono richieste eccellenti competenze in inglese. La nostra offerta Condurrai la tua ricerca nei laboratori di Empa a Dübendorf e sarai iscritto al programma di dottorato in Ingegneria Elettrica presso ETH Zurich. Il progetto fa parte del National Centre of Competence in Research (NCCR) Muoniverse ed è finanziato dalla Swiss National Science Foundation. Muoniverse collega oltre 30 gruppi di ricerca e offre una scuola di ricerca strutturata con formazione, opportunità di scambio e sviluppo di carriera. Siamo alla ricerca di candidati che amano la ricerca collaborativa, interdisciplinare e l'apertura del valore e il progresso condiviso. Muoniverse si impegna a pari opportunità, diversità e una cultura della ricerca inclusiva. Potrai condurre in modo indipendente esperimenti, tra cui studi di teletrasporto, collaborare con partner accademici e industriali, e diffondere i risultati attraverso pubblicazioni e presentazioni. I nostri laboratori forniscono l'accesso a un'ampia gamma di infrastrutture di ricerca della batteria, tra cui glovebox, forni, spettroscopia, microscopia e vasti impianti di test elettrochimici. La data di inizio è il 1 ottobre 2026 o su accordo. Empa si impegna per la diversità, l'equità e l'inclusione. Noi incoraggiamo fortemente le applicazioni da ricercatori e individui di sesso femminile da backgrounds sottorappresentati. Crediamo che la diversità spinga l'innovazione e l'eccellenza scientifica. Unisciti a noi per contribuire alla ricerca innovativa nelle tecnologie energetiche sostenibili! Non vediamo l'ora di ricevere la vostra domanda online, tra cui una lettera di motivazione di due pagine, CV, record accademici, diplomi con trascrizioni, e almeno due lettere di riferimento. Saranno considerate solo le applicazioni complete. Si prega di caricare tutti i documenti attraverso la nostra pagina web, le applicazioni via E-mail non possono essere accettate.

Materials science and technology are our passion. With our cutting-edge research, Empa's around 1,100 employees make essential contributions to the well-being of society for a future worth living. Empa is a research institution of the ETH Domain.

PhD Position on All-Solid-State Batteries

Empa’s Laboratory Materials for Energy Conversion focuses on materials and device innovation for sustainable energy technologies.

Your tasks

The aim of this PhD project is to investigate lithium- and sodium-based solid-state batteries using muon-based bulk and interface characterization techniques. The main objective is to gain a mechanistic understanding of electrochemical performance, with a focus on ion distribution, transport, and degradation processes during battery operation.
The project addresses key questions such as the formation of Li/Na concentration gradients during charge and discharge, the evolution of interphases, and degradation mechanisms including ageing, material dissolution (leaching), and transition-metal migration. Muon-based methods will be used to probe depth-resolved properties that are difficult to access with conventional techniques, enabling new insights into buried interfaces and bulk transport phenomena.

Your work will focus on electrochemical and structural characterization of battery materials and cells, combined with muon-based experiments. You will design and carry out experiments to identify reaction pathways and degradation mechanisms, and analyze complex datasets to connect microscopic processes with macroscopic performance. Close collaboration with project partners will support the development and testing of materials and cell concepts.

Your profile

You hold a Master’s degree in chemistry, materials science, or a related field, experience in electrochemistry or batteries is an advantage. Excellent English skills are required.

Our offer

You will conduct your research in Empa’s laboratories in Dübendorf and will be enrolled in the doctoral program in Electrical Engineering at ETH Zurich. The project is part of the National Centre of Competence in Research (NCCR) Muoniverse and is funded by the Swiss National Science Foundation.
Muoniverse connects over 30 research groups and offers a structured research school with training, exchange opportunities, and career development. We are looking for candidates who enjoy collaborative, interdisciplinary research and value openness and shared progress. Muoniverse is committed to equal opportunities, diversity, and an inclusive research culture.

You will independently conduct experiments, including muon beamline studies, collaborate with academic and industrial partners, and disseminate your results through publications and presentations. Our laboratories provide access to a broad range of battery research infrastructure, including gloveboxes, furnaces, spectroscopy, microscopy, and extensive electrochemical testing facilities.

Start date is October 1st, 2026 or upon agreement.

Empa is committed to diversity, equity, and inclusion. We strongly encourage applications from female researchers and individuals from underrepresented backgrounds. We believe diversity drives innovation and scientific excellence. Join us in contributing to groundbreaking research in sustainable energy technologies!

We look forward to receiving your online application including a two-page motivation letter, CV, scholarly records, diplomas with transcripts, and at least two reference letters. Only complete applications will be considered. Please upload all documents through our webpage, applications via E-mail cannot be accepted.

• Ihre Aufgaben Ziel dieses PhD-Projekts ist es, Lithium- und Natrium-basierte Festkörperbatterien unter Verwendung von Myonen-basierten Bulk- und Interface-Charakterisierungstechniken zu untersuchen. Muon-basierte Methoden werden verwendet, um tief aufgelöste Eigenschaften zu untersuchen, die mit herkömmlichen Techniken schwer zugänglich sind, was neue Einblicke in vergrabene Schnittstellen und Massentransportphänomene ermöglicht. Eine enge Zusammenarbeit mit den Projektpartnern wird die Entwicklung und Erprobung von Materialien und Zellkonzepten unterstützen. Sie werden unabhängig Experimente durchführen, einschließlich Myon Beamline-Studien, mit akademischen und industriellen Partnern zusammenarbeiten und Ihre Ergebnisse durch Publikationen und Präsentationen verbreiten. Unsere Labore bieten Zugang zu einer breiten Palette von Batterieforschungsinfrastrukturen, darunter Gloveboxen, Öfen, Spektroskopie, Mikroskopie und umfangreiche elektrochemische Prüfeinrichtungen. Position du doctorat sur les piles à l'état solide Les matériaux de laboratoire pour la conversion de l'énergie sont axés sur l'innovation des matériaux et des appareils pour les technologies énergétiques durables.
• Vos tâches Le but de ce projet de doctorat est d'étudier les batteries solides à base de lithium et de sodium à l'aide de techniques de caractérisation en vrac et d'interface à base de muon. L'objectif principal est d'acquérir une compréhension mécaniste de la performance électrochimique, en mettant l'accent sur la distribution des ions, le transport et les processus de dégradation pendant le fonctionnement de la batterie. Le projet aborde des questions clés telles que la formation de gradients de concentration de Li/Na pendant la charge et la décharge, l'évolution des interphases et les mécanismes de dégradation, y compris le vieillissement, la dissolution des matériaux (délavage) et la migration des métaux de transition. Des méthodes basées sur le muon seront utilisées pour sonder les propriétés résolues en profondeur qui sont difficiles d'accès avec les techniques conventionnelles, ce qui permettra de découvrir de nouvelles interfaces enfouies et des phénomènes de transport en vrac. Votre travail se concentrera sur la caractérisation électrochimique et structurale des matériaux et des cellules des batteries, combinée à des expériences basées sur le muon. Vous concevrez et réaliserez des expériences pour identifier les voies de réaction et les mécanismes de dégradation, et analyserez des ensembles de données complexes pour relier les processus microscopiques aux performances macroscopiques. Une collaboration étroite avec les partenaires du projet appuiera l'élaboration et l'essai de matériaux et de concepts cellulaires.

D'excellentes compétences en anglais sont requises. Muoniverse est attachée à l'égalité des chances, à la diversité et à une culture de recherche inclusive. Vous effectuerez des expériences indépendantes, y compris des études de faisceaux muon, collaborerez avec des partenaires universitaires et industriels, et diffuserez vos résultats au moyen de publications et de présentations. Nos laboratoires offrent un large éventail d'infrastructures de recherche sur les piles, notamment des boîtes à gants, des fours, de la spectroscopie, de la microscopie et de vastes installations d'essais électrochimiques. Rejoignez-nous pour contribuer à la recherche révolutionnaire sur les technologies énergétiques durables! Il laboratorio combina la produzione additiva, microprocessing laser su larga scala, modellazione multiscala e AI/ML per il monitoraggio/controllo di qualità, alla fine offrendo alla società nuovi materiali nanostrutturati, la loro forma-formatura e integrazione in dispositivi. • Funzionamento di diverse piattaforme laser
• Concettualizzazione e configurazione dei sistemi ottici
• Sincronizzazione hardware e acquisizione dati

Si lavorerà su un argomento scientificamente e tecnologicamente all'avanguardia di alta rilevanza e novità, con accesso diretto alle infrastrutture e attrezzature di ricerca all'avanguardia. descriptionByLocale.en:
Materials science and technology are our passion. With our cutting-edge research, Empa's around 1,100 employees make essential contributions to the well-being of society for a future worth living. Empa is a research institution of the ETH Domain.

Postdoc in applied laser physics

The Laboratory of Advanced Materials Processing (LAMP) is a multidisciplinary research unit that develops innovative functional modification of materials by beam (e.g. laser light, electrons) and plasma induced processing. LAMP provides full cycle technology development, starting from novel materials, deep understanding of the background physics of beam-matter interactions, development of automated AI/ML systems for novel materials processing and quality insurance. The lab combines additive manufacturing, large scale laser micro-processing, multiscale modelling and AI/ML for the quality monitoring/control, at the end offering to the society novel nanostructured materials, their shape-forming and integration into devices.

Your tasks

• Operation of different laser platforms

• Conceptualization and setup of optical systems

• Hardware synchronization and data acquisition

• Conduction of experimental campaigns, evaluation of results and reporting

Your profile

• PhD degree in Physics/Photonics/Engineering or equivalent

• Experience: Laser applications (measuring, processing, etc.), optical system design, assembly and usage

• Skills: Hands-on experimental mindset, strong understanding of laser and optical physics, strong problem-solving and troubleshooting skills, experience with data analysis and experimental optimization

• English, French and German as a plus

Our offer

Empa offers a dynamic and inspiring research environment at its Thun campus, located near Bern. You will work on a scientifically and technologically cutting-edge topic of high relevance and novelty, with direct access to state-of-the-art research infrastructure and equipment. As part of an experienced and multidisciplinary project team with strong national and international collaborations, you will receive full support in advancing the current project as well as in shaping and realizing your own scientific ideas within the lab's research activities. You will be encouraged and supported in producing high-impact results, publishing in leading international peer-reviewed journals, and pursuing your personal and professional development. The position is available with a starting date in September 2026 and a duration of one year with the possibility of extension.

We live a culture of inclusion and respect. We welcome all people who are interested in innovative, sustainable and meaningful activities - that's what counts.

We look forward to receiving your complete online application including a letter of motivation, CV, certificates, diplomas and contact details of two reference persons. Please submit these exclusively via our job portal. Applications by e-mail and by post will not be considered.

PostDoc in Computational Biology: Study of the crosstalk between the tumor and immune system in metastatic colorectal cancer

The group Multi-omics for Healthcare materials at Empa St. Gallen generates and integrates multi-modal biomedical datasets with the aim to inform development of new sensors, support nanoparticle-based cellular reprogramming strategies and identify new omics-based biomarkers. We work closely with clinical partners and we focus on deep understanding of molecular mechanisms of disease development.

Your tasks

We are looking for a highly motivated candidate with genuine interest in biomedicine and a strong proficiency in data analysis. In this project, we study how tumor-intrinsic genetic alterations and spatially organized microenvironmental niches jointly shape metastatic progression and therapy response in colorectal cancer. The project is strongly oriented towards clinical applications and identification of new therapeutic avenues.
The key responsibilities include:

• Working closely with interdisciplinary project partners

• Integrating newly generated datasets with multi-omics profiles of tumors from previous studies

• Developing new machine learning models through collaboration with the Swiss Data Science Centre

• Establishing data analysis pipelines, writing manuscripts and presenting at scientific conferences

Required qualifications include a PhD degree in computational biology or a related field. We are looking for a research-driven and results-oriented team player. Ideal profile includes following competencies and experience:
• Strong programming skills, deep statistical knowledge and a proven track record with machine learning

• Solid knowledge of tumor biology, signaling pathways and the tumor microenvironment

• Strong publication record

• Fluency in English and excellent communication and writing skills

• Experience in the analysis of single-cell and spatial transcriptomics datasets is desirable

This project was funded by the Swiss National Science Foundation and it allows close collaboration with the team of leading experts in the field as well as access to rich datasets generated on valuable clinical samples. Posizione del PhD in Graphene Nanoribbon dispositivi quantistici Il nanotech@surfaces Laboratory offre una posizione di PhD focalizzata sull'integrazione dei nanoribbons del grafo precisione atomica (GNRs) nelle eterostrutture di van der Waals in condizioni di vuoto ultra-alti. I GNR stanno emergendo materiali quantici la cui struttura elettronica, topologia e stati di rotazione possono essere progettati con precisione atomica, ma molti GNR reattivi si degradano durante i processi di trasferimento e fabbricazione substrato convenzionali. Il progetto mira a sviluppare un percorso di trasferimento completamente asciutto e compatibile con UHV che preserva questi fragili stati quantistici durante l'integrazione dei dispositivi.

Il lavoro combina strumentazione avanzata, assemblaggio 2D-materiale, spettroscopia Raman e STM/STS a bassa temperatura. Un obiettivo centrale è quello di indagare come le interfacce e gli ambienti elettrostatici influenzano le proprietà elettroniche e spin dei GNR trasferiti, progredendo da robusta poltrona GNRs a reattiva zigzag-edged e nanoribbons topologici che ospitano stati quantici correlati.
